question.text: Brahmaputra Debt Fund has received SEBI's in-principle approval for AIF registration while awaiting Trust Deed registration under the Registration Act, 1908. During this in-principle phase, the Manager may:

answer.text: Accept commitments from investors BUT shall NOT call or accept money until the Registration Certificate is granted; Trust Deed must be registered within 6 months of in-principle approval
Immediately call capital up to 50% and start deploying investments
Declare First Close within 15 days of in-principle approval
List the units on a recognised stock exchange for price discovery

explanation.text: The Logic: After in-principle approval, the applicant must ensure the Trust Deed or Partnership Deed is registered under the applicable law within 6 months from the date of in-principle approval, and the applicant may start accepting commitments from investors but shall not call or accept money until receipt of the Registration Certificate from SEBI. No investing, no First Close and no listing is permitted at this stage. The Trap: Option B jumps the gun on capital calls. Option C confuses in-principle approval with First Close declaration (which comes after registration and fundraising). Option D requires final close and SEBI listing-specific approval, which is not the in-principle phase. Note: Workbook pages 333 and 343 support the in-principle approval process, the 6-month deed-registration deadline and the no-capital-call rule.
